text:
I have been travelling across the Alps on trains a number of times and I have to say this is one of the most spectacular things you can do. But if you are going to do it, I think you need to really understand how it works. Why? Because the railway is a feat of engineering and the engineering is incredible. And the great thing is that when you're on a train, it is so smooth, it is so easy, and the views are so spectacular that you forget how hard it is. I mean, it is a mountain crossing. It's the sort of thing that for centuries was just impossible. And then in the 1800s, the engineers came along and said, well, we can actually do this. And they did it, and they did it beautifully.
So, how do they do it? Well, first of all, the journey starts in a city, probably. For example, the Bernina line goes from Chur in Switzerland down to Tirano in Italy. But the same thing is true of the Gotthard. So it starts in a city, and it's going to follow the valley up. And the idea of the valley is that it gives a gentle slope. That's the key. You want a gentle slope. And so it goes up the valley, it goes down the valley, it goes round the valley. It keeps going round and round and round. And the idea is that it's a gentle slope. It is not going to be a steep slope. And that is really important. That is really important because the railway needs to have a gentle slope. And if it is a steep slope, it is very difficult to negotiate. And the reason for that is that the wheels on the rails need to have friction. It's called adhesion. And if the slope is too steep, the wheels slip. And that's really dangerous. So you want to keep it gentle. And that's why it's all these long curves and spirals. And that's why the journey is so slow. It's slow because it's going round and round and round. And that's why it's so beautiful. Because you get to see the landscape.
And then you get to the part where it's really interesting. Because it has to cross the mountain. And so it has to go over the top, or it has to go through the mountain. And so it goes through the mountain. And that's where the tunnels come in. And the tunnels are really interesting. They are very, very long. And they are very, very expensive. And they are very, very difficult. And they take a very, very long time to build. But they are really, really cool. And they work really well. And it's a really amazing thing. And it is really nice to be in a tunnel, to be under the mountain. To be able to look up and see the rock, and to see the rock that you are going to come out of. And that is really cool. And then it's out. And it's the other side. And it's down the other side. And it's into another valley. And it's down, down, down. And then it's into another city.
